category: Physics interfaces III: AC/DC, RF, Wave Optics & Ray Optics features
description: Electromagnetic interfaces and features beyond the first EM chunk: the remaining AC/DC Module interfaces (Magnetic and Electric Fields, Rotating Machinery Magnetic, Electrical Circuit, Currents Only, shells, boundary elements) with their standard domain and boundary nodes (Ampere's Law, Magnetic Insulation, Ground, Electric Potential, Floating Potential, Force Calculation, Gauge Fixing, Periodic Condition), the RF and Wave Optics interfaces (Transient, Beam Envelopes, Transmission Line) and their ports, PEC/PMC, impedance and transition conditions, far-field calculation and scattered-field formulation, and the Ray Optics Geometrical Optics interface. API: model.component("comp1").physics().create(tag, type, "geom1") and physics(tag).create(ftag, type, dim).

tools.name: Magnetic and Electric Fields (mef)
tools.description: Solves for the magnetic vector potential A and the electric scalar potential V simultaneously, so that conductors driven by an applied voltage (rather than a total current) and capacitive-inductive interaction can be modelled in one interface. Use it for busbars and cables with terminals at given potentials, electrodes in conductive media with induced currents, and induction problems where the current distribution must follow from the voltage; for coils with a known current the Magnetic Fields (mf) interface alone is cheaper.
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Electromagnetic Fields > Magnetic and Electric Fields (mef); API: physics().create("mef", "ElectricInductionCurrents", "geom1")

parameters.name: Ampere's Law and Current Conservation
parameters.description: Default domain node combining the constitutive relations for B-H and J-E.

parameters.name: Terminal / Ground / Electric Potential
parameters.description: Boundary nodes that drive the conductors by voltage, current or circuit.

parameters.name: Magnetic Insulation / Electric Insulation
parameters.description: Default exterior conditions for A and V.

parameters.name: Gauge fixing
parameters.description: Often needed in stationary studies because V and A are coupled.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module. Frequency-domain solves are standard; stationary solves need gauge fixing or a Coulomb gauge via Magnetic Fields, Currents Only. The Magnetic Fields, No Currents + Electric Currents combination cannot capture induced currents - that is where mef is needed.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Magnetic (rmm)
tools.description: Magnetic Fields interface pre-configured for machines with a rotor turning inside a stator: it combines vector-potential (A) and scalar-potential formulations per domain, a Rotating Domain moving-mesh feature and a sector/continuity pair condition on the sliding air-gap boundary created by Form Assembly. Used for motors, generators, magnetic couplings and eddy-current brakes in 2D, 2D axisymmetric (for axial machines) and 3D, in stationary parametric sweeps over rotor angle or time-dependent runs.
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Electromagnetic Fields > Rotating Machinery, Magnetic (rmm); API: physics().create("rmm", "RotatingMachineryMagnetic", "geom1")

parameters.name: Rotating Domain (Definitions > Moving Mesh)
parameters.description: Rotor domains and rotational velocity (rpm) or angle.

parameters.name: Continuity / Sector Symmetry pair feature
parameters.description: Applied on the identity pair of the air-gap interface.

parameters.name: Ampere's Law / Magnetic Flux Conservation
parameters.description: Per-domain formulation choice; use scalar potential where there are no currents.

parameters.name: Coil / Permanent magnet (Ampere's Law > Remanent flux density)
parameters.description: Sources on stator windings and rotor magnets.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module and Form Assembly with an identity pair on the air gap; keep the air gap split by a circular boundary inside the gap and mesh both sides similarly. Torque is evaluated with the Force Calculation node or Arkkio's method (rmm.Tark).

tools.name: Electrical Circuit (cir)
tools.description: Zero-dimensional interface for lumped circuit elements - resistors, capacitors, inductors, voltage/current sources, controlled sources, diodes, transistors, switches, transformers, subcircuits and SPICE netlist import - solved together with the finite-element interfaces. Terminals, coils, lumped ports and electrode features can be set to 'Circuit' type so a field model becomes one element in the circuit (External I vs. U, External U vs. I, External I-terminal nodes on the circuit side).
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Electrical Circuit (cir); API: physics().create("cir", "Circuit", "geom1"); cir.create("R1", "Resistor", -1)

parameters.name: Node names
parameters.description: Circuit nodes are integers; 0 is ground.

parameters.name: Element types
parameters.description: Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, VoltageSource, CurrentSource, Diode, NPN/PNP BJT, MOSFET, Transformer, Mutual Inductance, Switch, Subcircuit.

parameters.name: External I vs. U / External U vs. I / External I-Terminal
parameters.description: Couplings to a Terminal, Coil, Lumped Port or Electrode of another interface.

parameters.name: SPICE import
parameters.description: Import SPICE netlist reads .cir files into circuit nodes.

tools.notes: Included in AC/DC, RF, MEMS, Plasma, Semiconductor and Battery modules. Circuit variables are cir.R1_v, cir.R1_i etc. Time-dependent circuits with switches need small time steps or event handling; frequency-domain circuits are linear.

tools.name: Magnetic Fields, Currents Only (mfco)
tools.description: Interface that computes the stationary current distribution in conductors (with a Coulomb-gauge formulation for A) and the resulting magnetic field without needing to mesh the surrounding air with magnetic properties, intended for extracting resistance and inductance matrices of interconnects, PCB traces and busbars, and as the current source for a subsequent Magnetic Fields solve. Runs with the Stationary Source Sweep study to build the full L and R matrices automatically.
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Electromagnetic Fields > Magnetic Fields, Currents Only (mfco); API: physics().create("mfco", "MagneticFieldsCurrentsOnly", "geom1")

parameters.name: Conductor
parameters.description: Domain node with conductivity; the surrounding air needs no properties.

parameters.name: Terminal
parameters.description: Current, voltage or circuit excitation on conductor end faces.

parameters.name: Stationary Source Sweep
parameters.description: Study step that excites each terminal in turn and assembles L and R matrices (mfco.L11...).

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module (5.5+). Only for DC/low-frequency partial inductance with negligible skin effect; use mf or mef in the frequency domain for AC losses.

tools.name: Electric Currents in Shells (ecs)
tools.description: Boundary (shell) version of Electric Currents that solves current conservation on surfaces with a given thickness, so thin conducting layers - PCB copper, electrodes on insulators, metallization on MEMS, coated films - need no volumetric mesh. Works in 3D on boundaries and in 2D on edges, and couples to Electric Currents domains through Electric Shielding / thin-layer features or shared boundaries.
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Electric Fields and Currents > Electric Currents in Shells (ecs); API: physics().create("ecs", "ElectricCurrentsShell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Current Conservation (shell)
parameters.description: Boundary node with conductivity and layer thickness ds.

parameters.name: Electric Potential / Ground / Terminal (edge)
parameters.description: Excitations applied on edges of the shell.

parameters.name: Layered material support
parameters.description: Thickness and properties can come from a Layered Material.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module. Joule heating of a shell couples to Heat Transfer in Shells; for thick layers with through-thickness gradients use volumetric Electric Currents.

tools.name: Electrostatics, Boundary Elements (esbe)
tools.description: Boundary element method (BEM) formulation of electrostatics that requires only the surfaces of conductors and dielectric interfaces to be meshed, treating the surrounding space as an infinite (or half-space) homogeneous medium. Ideal for capacitance of objects in open air, electrode arrays and large empty regions; it can be coupled to the FEM Electrostatics interface with the Electrostatics, Boundary Elements-FEM coupling for detailed dielectric parts.
tools.usage: Add Physics > AC/DC > Electric Fields and Currents > Electrostatics, Boundary Elements (esbe); API: physics().create("esbe", "ElectrostaticsBoundaryElements", "geom1")

parameters.name: Charge Conservation (domain, infinite void)
parameters.description: Permittivity of the unbounded medium; select the void domain or an infinite void.

parameters.name: Electric Potential / Terminal / Ground
parameters.description: Conditions on BEM boundaries.

parameters.name: Symmetry/Infinite ground plane
parameters.description: Options for half-space problems.

parameters.name: Solver
parameters.description: Uses a dense/iterative BEM solver with ACA compression; set in the Iterative node.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module (5.3+). BEM matrices are dense; memory grows with the square of boundary elements, so keep surface meshes coarse. Magnetic Fields, No Currents, Boundary Elements (mfncbe) is the magnetostatic analogue.

tools.name: Ground
tools.description: Boundary (or edge/point) condition setting the electric potential V = 0. Every Electrostatics, Electric Currents, Magnetic and Electric Fields or electrochemistry model needs a ground (or a voltage-type terminal) somewhere so that the potential is unique; it is also the natural reference for terminals and floating potentials.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrostatics/Electric Currents > Ground (gnd1); API: physics("es").create("gnd1", "Ground", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries (3D) / edges (2D) forced to V = 0.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Apply reaction terms, use weak constraints (for accurate reaction currents).

tools.notes: In Electric Currents the current through a grounded boundary is available via reaction forces (reacf(V)) or the Terminal node with Ground type - use a Terminal of type Voltage 0 when you need the current as a variable (ec.I0_1).

tools.name: Electric Potential
tools.description: Boundary, edge or point condition prescribing V = V0, a Dirichlet condition for the electric potential. Use it for electrodes at a known voltage when you do not need the terminal bookkeeping (current, capacitance matrix) that the Terminal node provides; V0 may be a function of time, frequency or position.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrostatics/Electric Currents > Electric Potential (pot1); API: physics("es").create("pot1", "ElectricPotential", 2); set("V0", ...)

parameters.name: V0
parameters.description: Prescribed potential expression, e.g. 1[kV]*rm1(t[1/s]) or V0*exp(-j*phi).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Entities constrained.

tools.notes: Terminal (Voltage type) gives the same constraint plus lumped quantities and terminal sweeps; Floating Potential is the counterpart for conductors with unknown but uniform potential.

tools.name: Floating Potential
tools.description: Boundary condition for an electrically isolated conductor whose potential is uniform but unknown: it constrains V to a single floating value on the selection and specifies the total charge (Electrostatics) or total current (Electric Currents) on it, usually zero. Used for ungrounded metal parts, guard rings, floating gates, unconnected electrodes and shields.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrostatics/Electric Currents > Floating Potential (fp1); API: physics("es").create("fp1", "FloatingPotential", 2)

parameters.name: Q0 / I0
parameters.description: Total charge (es) or total current (ec) on the floating conductor, default 0.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: Several boundaries can share one floating potential by belonging to the same node.

parameters.name: Circuit connection
parameters.description: Can be connected to an Electrical Circuit node.

tools.notes: Each Floating Potential adds one global DOF; the value is available as es.V0_<tag>. Terminal with Terminated or Charge type is the alternative when you need a matrix extraction.

tools.name: Ampere's Law
tools.description: Default domain node of Magnetic Fields (and the magnetic part of mef/rmm) that holds the constitutive relations: the B-H relation (relative permeability, B-H curve, remanent flux density for permanent magnets, magnetization, effective B-H, hysteresis Jiles-Atherton), the J-E relation (conductivity, linearized resistivity) and the D-E relation. Add extra Ampere's Law nodes to give different domains different material models (e.g. magnets with remanence).
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields > Ampere's Law (al1 default; add more with right-click); API: physics("mf").create("al2", "AmperesLaw", 3)

parameters.name: Constitutive relation B-H
parameters.description: RelativePermeability | BHCurve | RemanentFluxDensity | Magnetization | EffectiveBHCurve | HysteresisJilesAtherton.

parameters.name: Br / e_Br
parameters.description: Remanent flux density magnitude and direction for permanent magnets.

parameters.name: Conductivity model
parameters.description: From material, linearized resistivity (temperature dependent), or user defined.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: For anisotropic laminations.

tools.notes: In 6.x the AC/DC Module material library ships B-H curves for many steels (Nonlinear Magnetic library) and the Effective B-H option handles time-harmonic saturation. Magnetic Flux Conservation is the equivalent node of the scalar-potential interface mfnc.

tools.name: Magnetic Insulation
tools.description: Default exterior boundary condition of the A-formulation, n x A = 0, which makes the boundary a magnetic flux line (tangential magnetic field only, no flux crossing) and is also a perfect electric conductor for induced currents. Correct for symmetry planes where B is tangential and as a far boundary of a sufficiently large air box; for the opposite symmetry (B normal to the plane) use Perfect Magnetic Conductor.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields > Magnetic Insulation (mi1 default); API: physics("mf").create("mi2", "MagneticInsulation", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries where n x A = 0.

tools.notes: Placing magnetic insulation too close to a device compresses the field and overestimates inductance; use Infinite Element Domains or a box several device sizes large. Magnetic Fields, No Currents has the analogous Magnetic Insulation (n.B = 0) and Zero Magnetic Scalar Potential nodes.

tools.name: Magnetic Flux Conservation
tools.description: Default domain node of Magnetic Fields, No Currents (mfnc): it solves div(B) = 0 with B derived from a magnetic scalar potential Vm and carries the B-H constitutive relation (permeability, B-H curve, remanent flux density for magnets, magnetization). Add nodes per material region; the interface is the cheapest way to model permanent-magnet assemblies, magnetic shielding and yokes when there are no currents or eddy currents.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Magnetic Flux Conservation (mfc1); API: physics("mfnc").create("mfc2", "MagneticFluxConservation", 3)

parameters.name: Constitutive relation B-H
parameters.description: Relative permeability, B-H curve, remanent flux density, magnetization, effective B-H.

parameters.name: Br
parameters.description: Remanent flux density vector for permanent magnets.

tools.notes: The scalar potential cannot represent a region enclosing a net current (multiply connected domains with coils) - use mf for those or the Reduced Field formulation with a background field. Coupling to mf domains is possible through the Magnetic Fields / No Currents mixed formulation.

tools.name: External Current Density
tools.description: Domain node in Magnetic Fields adding a prescribed current density Je (A/m^2) as a source, for currents whose distribution is known analytically (uniform in a wire cross-section, a rotating field from three-phase windings written as expressions, currents imported from another study via withsol/General Extrusion). It is the manual alternative to the Coil node, which computes the density from a total current and geometry.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields > External Current Density (ecd1); API: physics("mf").create("ecd1", "ExternalCurrentDensity", 3)

parameters.name: Je
parameters.description: Current density vector components, e.g. {0, 0, I0/A_wire} or {-J0*sin(phi), J0*cos(phi), 0}.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Cylindrical systems make azimuthal currents easy to express.

tools.notes: The prescribed density must be divergence free in 3D or the solution is ill-posed; the Coil feature with Coil Geometry Analysis guarantees this automatically.

tools.name: Force Calculation
tools.description: Domain node that integrates the Maxwell stress tensor over the exterior boundary of the selected domains to give the total electromagnetic force and torque on them (variables mf.Forcex_<name>, mf.Tax_<name>, or es.Forcex_ for electrostatics). Used for actuator forces, magnetic bearing stiffness, motor torque, MEMS comb-drive force and radiation pressure; several nodes can be added for different bodies.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields / Electrostatics > Force Calculation (fcal1); API: physics("mf").create("fcal1", "ForceCalculation", 3)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: The body (domains) the force acts on; must be surrounded by non-magnetic/air domains for accuracy.

parameters.name: Force name
parameters.description: Suffix used in the variable names (default the tag).

parameters.name: Torque axis / rotation point
parameters.description: Reference for torque evaluation.

parameters.name: Time-average / cycle-averaged forces
parameters.description: Frequency-domain models also give averaged force variables (mf.Forcex_av_...).

tools.notes: Stress-tensor forces are mesh sensitive: refine the air mesh around the body and avoid placing the body's boundary coincident with material interfaces. Arkkio's method (rmm) and the Lorentz-force body load (solid: Electromagnetic Forces coupling) are the alternatives.

tools.name: Gauge Fixing for A-field
tools.description: Domain node that adds a scalar Lagrange-multiplier field psi and the constraint div(A) = 0 (Coulomb gauge), removing the null space of the curl-curl operator so that stationary magnetostatic problems with curl elements have a unique solution and iterative solvers converge. Needed when a model contains non-conducting domains in a stationary study or when the solver stalls; not needed in most frequency-domain problems where conductivity regularises the system.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields > Gauge Fixing for A-field (gfx1); API: physics("mf").create("gfx1", "GaugeFixing", 3)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: All domains normally; must be connected.

parameters.name: Equation form / divergence condition
parameters.description: Automatic or explicit weak/strong form.

parameters.name: Divergence condition variable scaling
parameters.description: Scaling factor for psi to improve conditioning.

tools.notes: Gauge fixing increases DOFs and makes the system saddle-point; the direct solver usually copes, and the default iterative solver for mf uses a suitable preconditioner. In 6.x the solver often converges without it thanks to improved defaults; try without first for large 3D models.

tools.name: Periodic Condition (electromagnetics)
tools.description: Boundary condition linking a source and a destination boundary so the fields repeat (continuity), change sign (antiperiodicity) or acquire a Floquet/Bloch phase shift given by a k-vector (RF/Wave Optics) or a sector angle (rotating machinery). Reduces periodic structures - motor pole pitches, metamaterial unit cells, gratings, phased arrays - to one cell; the meshes on both sides should be copied (Mesh > Copy Face) for accuracy.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields / Electromagnetic Waves > Periodic Condition (pc1); API: physics("emw").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2); set("PeriodicType", "Floquet")

parameters.name: PeriodicType
parameters.description: Continuity | Antiperiodicity | Floquet | Cyclic symmetry (sector angle).

parameters.name: kFloquet
parameters.description: Floquet wave vector, often taken from a Port (emw.kperiodic...).

parameters.name: Destination selection
parameters.description: Automatic detection or manual destination boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires geometrically congruent boundaries; in 6.x the destination is found automatically. Combine with a Periodic Port for grating/diffraction-order problems. Heat transfer, structural and acoustics have their own Periodic Condition nodes with the same source/destination logic.

tools.name: Electric Insulation
tools.description: Default exterior boundary condition of Electric Currents, n.J = 0, meaning no current leaves through the boundary; also the right condition on symmetry planes parallel to the current flow and on interfaces to non-conducting surroundings that are not modelled. In Electrostatics the analogous default is Zero Charge (n.D = 0).
tools.usage: Physics > Electric Currents > Electric Insulation (ein1 default); API: physics("ec").create("ein2", "ElectricInsulation", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries with zero normal current.

tools.notes: Interior boundaries between conducting domains are continuous by default; to insulate them use Thin Low Permittivity Gap / Contact Impedance or Electric Shielding (thin conductive layer).

tools.name: Surface Charge Density
tools.description: Electrostatics boundary condition specifying a surface charge rho_s, giving the jump n.(D1 - D2) = rho_s across an interior boundary or n.D = rho_s on an exterior one. Used for charged membranes, electret films, trapped interface charge in semiconductors/MEMS and triboelectric charging.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrostatics > Surface Charge Density (scd1); API: physics("es").create("scd1", "SurfaceChargeDensity", 2)

parameters.name: rhoqs
parameters.description: Surface charge density expression (C/m^2).

tools.notes: Space Charge Density is the domain version; Electric Displacement Field prescribes n.D directly.

tools.name: Boundary Current Source
tools.description: Electric Currents boundary condition injecting a normal current density Qj (A/m^2) on an interior or exterior boundary - the current analogue of Surface Charge Density. Used to model current injected by an electrode whose interior is not meshed, thin current-carrying films, or a distributed current source from another physics (e.g. an electrochemical reaction rate).
tools.usage: Physics > Electric Currents > Boundary Current Source (bcs1); API: physics("ec").create("bcs1", "BoundaryCurrentSource", 2)

parameters.name: Qjs
parameters.description: Boundary current source density expression.

tools.notes: Normal Current Density is the exterior-boundary form; Current Source is the domain (A/m^3) version; Terminal with Current type prescribes a total current instead of a density.

tools.name: Magnetic Shielding
tools.description: Boundary condition in Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Fields, No Currents that represents a thin layer of high-permeability material (mu-metal shield, steel sheet) of thickness ds as a surface with tangential flux conduction, so the sheet need not be meshed through its thickness. Complementary features are Thin Low Permeability Gap (air gaps in cores) and Transition Boundary Condition (conductive sheets with eddy currents).
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields > Magnetic Shielding (ms1); API: physics("mf").create("ms1", "MagneticShielding", 2)

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Layer thickness.

parameters.name: Constitutive relation
parameters.description: Relative permeability or B-H curve of the shielding material.

tools.notes: Valid while the sheet is thin compared with the surrounding geometry and not saturated; for saturating shields use a B-H curve or mesh the sheet.

tools.name: Impedance Boundary Condition (mf)
tools.description: Magnetic Fields boundary condition for the frequency domain that models a good conductor whose interior need not be meshed: it relates tangential E and H through the surface impedance of the material (skin depth much smaller than the object), returning the surface loss density for induction heating and shielding. It removes the need to resolve the skin depth with boundary layers in thick conductors.
tools.usage: Physics > Magnetic Fields > Impedance Boundary Condition (ibc1); API: physics("mf").create("ibc1", "ImpedanceBoundaryCondition", 2)

parameters.name: Material (conductivity, permeability, permittivity)
parameters.description: Of the excluded conductor; From material of the adjacent (removed) domain or user defined.

parameters.name: Surface roughness / layered options
parameters.description: Corrections for loss (6.x).

tools.notes: Accuracy requires skin depth < ~1/5 of the curvature radius and thickness; at low frequency or for thin sheets use the Transition Boundary Condition instead. The RF interface has its own Impedance Boundary Condition with the same idea for microwave cavities and waveguides.

tools.name: Charge Conservation
tools.description: Default domain node of Electrostatics holding the D-E constitutive relation: relative permittivity (isotropic/anisotropic), polarization, remanent displacement, dielectric loss (loss tangent, complex permittivity in the frequency domain) or dispersion models. Add nodes for piezoelectric/ferroelectric or lossy domains; Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric is created automatically by the Piezoelectricity multiphysics interface.
tools.usage: Physics > Electrostatics > Charge Conservation (ccn1 default); API: physics("es").create("ccn2", "ChargeConservation", 3)

parameters.name: Constitutive relation D-E
parameters.description: RelativePermittivity | Polarization | RemanentDisplacement | LossTangent | DielectricLoss | Dispersion.

parameters.name: epsilonr
parameters.description: Relative permittivity value or tensor.

tools.notes: Current Conservation is the Electric Currents counterpart (sigma and epsilon_r). Space Charge Density adds a volumetric source rho_v.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (temw)
tools.description: Time-domain full-wave interface solving the wave equation for the magnetic vector potential A with curl elements, for problems that are nonlinear, broadband, or involve time-varying media: pulse propagation, nonlinear optics (second-harmonic generation, Kerr effect), transient EMI/EMP, TDR of transmission structures and time-domain reflectometry. Excited with lumped ports, scattering boundaries carrying an incident pulse, or edge currents; results can be transformed with the Time to Frequency FFT study.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Radio Frequency / Wave Optics > Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (temw); API: physics().create("temw", "TransientElectromagneticWaves", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wave Equation, Electric
parameters.description: Domain node with epsilon_r, mu_r, sigma and nonlinear polarization options.

parameters.name: Scattering Boundary Condition / Lumped Port
parameters.description: Absorbing boundary and excitation with time-dependent amplitude (e.g. a Gaussian pulse function).

parameters.name: Time-Dependent Solver settings
parameters.description: Generalized alpha with strict steps of ~1/(20 f_max) and CFL-consistent mesh (~5 elements per shortest wavelength).

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module or Wave Optics Module. Much more expensive than a frequency-domain sweep for linear problems; use it only when the frequency domain cannot represent the physics. The Electromagnetic Waves, Time Explicit (teew) interface (discontinuous Galerkin) is preferred for very large linear time-domain problems.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes (ewbe)
tools.description: Wave Optics interface that factors the electric field into a slowly varying envelope times a known fast phase, E = E1 exp(-j k1.r) (+ E2 exp(-j k2.r) for bidirectional propagation), so the mesh only has to resolve the envelope rather than the wavelength. It makes waveguides, fibres, directional couplers, laser cavities, lens systems and nonlinear crystals that are thousands of wavelengths long tractable, provided the propagation direction(s) are known in advance; strongly scattering problems must use the Frequency Domain interface.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Wave Optics > Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes (ewbe); API: physics().create("ewbe", "ElectromagneticWavesBeamEnvelopes", "geom1")

parameters.name: Number of directions
parameters.description: Unidirectional or bidirectional envelope.

parameters.name: Wave vector k1 (k2)
parameters.description: User defined, from a Port's mode analysis, or from a computed phase (Phase Initialization study).

parameters.name: Port / Matched Boundary Condition
parameters.description: Excitation and absorbing conditions consistent with the envelope formulation.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: Coarse along propagation (element size set by envelope variation), fine transversally.

tools.notes: Requires the Wave Optics Module. Combine with a Boundary Mode Analysis study step to get the port mode and the exact propagation constant for k1. Laser Heating multiphysics couples ewbe to Heat Transfer.

tools.name: Transmission Line (tl)
tools.description: 1D/2D/3D-edge interface solving the telegrapher's equations for voltage and current along lines characterised by distributed R, L, G, C per unit length, for cable networks, microstrip/stripline interconnects, matching networks and lumped-element loaded lines in the frequency domain. Terminal features (Lumped Port, Terminating Impedance, Open Circuit, Short Circuit) give S-parameters; the line parameters can come from a 2D cross-section mode analysis.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Radio Frequency > Transmission Line (tl); API: physics().create("tl", "TransmissionLine", "geom1")

parameters.name: Transmission Line Equation
parameters.description: Domain/edge node with R, L, G, C per unit length.

parameters.name: Lumped Port / Terminating Impedance
parameters.description: Excitation and load at line ends; Z0 reference impedance.

parameters.name: Incoming Wave / Absorbing Boundary
parameters.description: Matched terminations.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module. Only the fundamental TEM/quasi-TEM mode is represented; use full 3D emw when higher-order modes or radiation matter. Line parameters for a given cross-section: run a 2D Mode Analysis with emw and read emw.Z0 / beta.

tools.name: Port (rectangular / coaxial / circular / numeric / periodic)
tools.description: Waveguide-type excitation and absorption boundary for Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain and Beam Envelopes: a Port prescribes the transverse mode field (analytic for rectangular TE/TM, coaxial TEM and circular modes, computed by a Boundary Mode Analysis for Numeric ports, or diffraction orders for Periodic ports), injects a given power or amplitude when 'Wave excitation at this port' is on, and absorbs the outgoing part of that mode. S-parameters (emw.S11, emw.S21dB...) are computed between all ports and a Frequency Domain Source Sweep can excite each port in turn.
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Port (port1); API: physics("emw").create("port1", "Port", 2); set("PortType", "Rectangular"|"Coaxial"|"Circular"|"Numeric"|"Periodic"|"UserDefined")

parameters.name: PortType
parameters.description: Rectangular | Coaxial | Circular | Numeric | Periodic | User defined | Domain-backed (6.x).

parameters.name: PortExcitation / Pin
parameters.description: on/off and input power (W) or deposited/voltage options.

parameters.name: Mode type / mode number
parameters.description: TE/TM and indices for analytic ports; Numeric ports take the mode from the Boundary Mode Analysis step.

parameters.name: Slit condition
parameters.description: Interior port (activate slit) for ports inside the domain with a PML behind.

parameters.name: Diffraction Order subnodes
parameters.description: For Periodic ports: listing of higher orders with their own S-parameters.

tools.notes: Requires the RF or Wave Optics Module. A Numeric port needs one Boundary Mode Analysis study step per port with the port name set; the resulting propagation constant is emw.beta_port2. Lumped Port (already catalogued) is the low-frequency/TEM alternative that needs no mode.

tools.name: Perfect Electric Conductor
tools.description: Default exterior boundary condition of the RF/Wave Optics wave interfaces, n x E = 0, representing a lossless metal wall: waveguide walls, cavity walls, ground planes, antenna metal and symmetry planes where E is normal. It carries no loss; use Impedance Boundary Condition for finite conductivity losses (Q factors, attenuation).
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves > Perfect Electric Conductor (pec1 default); API: physics("emw").create("pec2", "PerfectElectricConductor", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Metal boundaries and E-normal symmetry planes.

tools.notes: Interior PEC boundaries split the domain electrically (a thin metal plate). Surface currents are available as emw.Jsx etc. Perfect Magnetic Conductor is the dual (n x H = 0) for H-normal symmetry planes.

tools.name: Perfect Magnetic Conductor
tools.description: Boundary condition n x H = 0 (tangential magnetic field vanishes), the dual of PEC. It has no physical realisation as a material but is the correct symmetry condition on planes where the electric field is tangential (magnetic wall), halving or quartering antenna, waveguide and cavity models; it is also used as an artificial 'open' wall in some periodic structures.
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves > Perfect Magnetic Conductor (pmc1); API: physics("emw").create("pmc1", "PerfectMagneticConductor", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Symmetry planes with tangential E.

tools.notes: Choosing PEC vs PMC on a symmetry plane depends on the polarization of the excited mode; the wrong one suppresses the mode entirely. Port power must be halved for each symmetry plane if you compare with a full model.

tools.name: Impedance Boundary Condition (emw)
tools.description: RF/Wave Optics boundary condition for lossy metal walls whose interior need not be meshed: it imposes the Leontovich surface impedance sqrt(mu/(epsilon - j sigma/omega)) relation between tangential E and H, giving realistic wall losses, cavity Q factors, waveguide attenuation and plasmonic metal surfaces. Options include a thin dielectric coating on the conductor and surface roughness loss models.
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Impedance Boundary Condition (imp1); API: physics("emw").create("imp1", "Impedance", 2)

parameters.name: Material properties
parameters.description: epsilon_r, mu_r, sigma of the excluded conductor (from material or user).

parameters.name: Surface roughness
parameters.description: Model (e.g. Hammerstad, Huray) and RMS roughness for PCB copper (6.x).

parameters.name: Thin layer
parameters.description: Optional dielectric coating thickness.

tools.notes: Valid when the skin depth is much smaller than the conductor thickness and curvature radius. Transition Boundary Condition covers thin sheets where both faces interact.

tools.name: Transition Boundary Condition
tools.description: Boundary condition representing a thin conductive or dielectric sheet of thickness d (metal foil, ITO film, thin absorber, patterned metallization, graphene) as an interior boundary with surface currents on both faces coupled through the sheet impedance, so the film's thickness never has to be meshed. Available in Magnetic Fields (frequency domain) and the wave interfaces; the film can be layered (Layered Material) in 6.x.
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves / Magnetic Fields > Transition Boundary Condition (tbc1); API: physics("emw").create("tbc1", "TransitionBoundaryCondition", 2)

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Sheet thickness.

parameters.name: Material properties
parameters.description: epsilon_r, mu_r, sigma of the film.

parameters.name: Electric thickness options
parameters.description: Automatic / user-defined surface impedance.

tools.notes: Unlike the Impedance Boundary Condition it handles films thinner than the skin depth and transmits fields through the sheet. For frequency-selective surfaces with fine patterns, mesh the pattern in the boundary and apply the condition on the metal faces only.

tools.name: Far-Field Domain / Far-Field Calculation
tools.description: Far-Field Domain is a domain node (usually the air region inside the PML) that adds a Far-Field Calculation boundary subnode on its exterior boundary; the subnode applies the Stratton-Chu near-to-far-field transformation and defines the far-field variables emw.Efarx, emw.normEfar, emw.normdBEfar, gain and axial ratio used by the Radiation Pattern (Far Field) plots and antenna directivity/gain evaluation. Antenna, RCS and scattering models need it to get radiation patterns without extending the mesh to the far zone.
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Far-Field Domain (ffd1) > Far-Field Calculation (ffc1); API: physics("emw").create("ffd1", "FarFieldDomain", 3); feature("ffd1").feature("ffc1").selection().set(...)

parameters.name: Far-Field Domain selection
parameters.description: Air domains enclosing the radiator (not the PML).

parameters.name: Far-Field Calculation boundaries
parameters.description: Closed surface where the transformation is evaluated (exterior of the far-field domain by default).

parameters.name: Symmetry settings
parameters.description: Declare PEC/PMC symmetry planes so the pattern of the full structure is reconstructed.

parameters.name: Far-field variable name
parameters.description: Suffix for Efar variables when several nodes exist.

tools.notes: Requires the RF or Wave Optics Module. The calculation surface must not touch the PML or a PEC ground plane (use the symmetry options for infinite ground planes). Pressure Acoustics has the analogous Exterior Field Calculation.

tools.name: Wave Equation, Electric
tools.description: Default domain node of Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain / Transient that holds the material models for the wave equation: relative permittivity (or refractive index n, k for optics), loss tangent, conductivity, Drude-Lorentz/Debye/Sellmeier dispersion, anisotropic tensors, and in 6.x also nonlinear (Kerr, second-order) and gyrotropic models. Add extra nodes when different domains need different model types (e.g. refractive index for glass, Drude for metal).
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Wave Equation, Electric (wee1 default); API: physics("emw").create("wee2", "WaveEquationElectric", 3)

parameters.name: Electric displacement field model
parameters.description: RelativePermittivity | RefractiveIndex | LossTangent | DielectricLoss | DrudeLorentz | Debye | Sellmeier | Polarization.

parameters.name: epsilonr / n, ki
parameters.description: Permittivity or refractive index and extinction coefficient.

parameters.name: sigma, mur
parameters.description: Conductivity and permeability.

tools.notes: The Optical material library (Wave Optics/Ray Optics) provides n(lambda) for glasses and metals as interpolation functions. Mesh ~5-6 second-order elements per wavelength in the material with the highest n.

tools.name: Scattered Field Formulation (background field)
tools.description: Interface-level setting of Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain that splits the total field into a user-specified background field (plane wave, Gaussian beam, or a field from another solution) plus the scattered field that is solved for, so a scatterer illuminated from infinity can be modelled with a PML absorbing only the scattered part. Standard setup for radar cross-section, nanoparticle scattering/absorption cross-sections, and optical scattering off gratings and defects.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain settings > Formulation: Scattered field, Background electric field: E_b expressions; API: physics("emw").prop("BackgroundField").set("SolveFor", "scatteredField"); set("Eb", {...})

parameters.name: SolveFor
parameters.description: fullField | scatteredField.

parameters.name: Background wave type
parameters.description: User defined expressions, Gaussian beam (paraxial or exact), or Linearly polarized plane wave (6.x).

parameters.name: Eb
parameters.description: Background field, e.g. {0, 0, E0*exp(-j*emw.k0*x)}.

tools.notes: The background field must satisfy the wave equation in the homogeneous surrounding medium; with a substrate use the Fresnel-reflected field or a two-step model. Absorption cross-section = integral of emw.Qh over the particle divided by incident intensity.

tools.name: Surface Current Density (emw)
tools.description: Boundary condition prescribing a surface current Js on a boundary of the wave interfaces (or Magnetic Fields), used as a simple source for antennas, current sheets modelling patch feeds, and for imposing known currents from circuit models. In Magnetic Fields the analogous node is Surface Current Density with the same role.
tools.usage: Physics > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Surface Current Density (scu1); API: physics("emw").create("scu1", "SurfaceCurrent", 2)

parameters.name: Js0
parameters.description: Surface current density vector (A/m).

tools.notes: Edge Current and Magnetic Current are the line/dual sources; Lumped Port is normally preferred for feeds because it yields impedance and S-parameters.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements (embe)
tools.description: BEM formulation of the frequency-domain Maxwell equations for lossless or lossy homogeneous domains that meshes only surfaces and treats the exterior as infinite, eliminating PMLs and air meshes for antenna arrays, scattering from large metallic objects and radiation into free space. Typically used coupled to the FEM Electromagnetic Waves interface (Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements-FEM coupling) with FEM handling the inhomogeneous parts (feeds, dielectrics).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Radio Frequency > Electromagnetic Waves, Boundary Elements (embe); API: physics().create("embe", "ElectromagneticWavesBoundaryElements", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wave Equation (infinite void)
parameters.description: Material of the unbounded medium.

parameters.name: PEC / Impedance boundaries
parameters.description: Metal surfaces modelled by BEM.

parameters.name: Far field
parameters.description: Radiation pattern variables are available directly (embe.normEfar) without a Far-Field Domain.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module (5.4+). BEM cost scales with surface elements squared unless the iterative ACA-compressed solver is used (default); electrically very large objects are still expensive. The API type string in this entry could not be confirmed in the COMSOL 6.4 registry; confirm it with Model Builder > File > Save As > Model File for Java.

tools.name: Geometrical Optics (gop)
tools.description: Ray Optics Module interface that traces rays through geometry with position-dependent refractive index, computing trajectories, intensity, polarization, phase, optical path length and monochromatic aberrations, with rays refracting/reflecting at material discontinuities, absorbed by walls, split at partially reflecting surfaces, and interacting with gratings, thin dielectric films and mirrors. Used for lens and mirror systems, solar concentrators, laser cavities, illumination and, coupled with heat transfer and structural mechanics, thermo-optic and stress-optic effects (Ray Heating multiphysics).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Optics > Ray Optics > Geometrical Optics (gop); API: physics().create("gop", "GeometricalOptics", "geom1"); study: Ray Tracing

parameters.name: Medium Properties
parameters.description: Domain node with refractive index (real and imaginary), optionally from the Optical material library or temperature dependent.

parameters.name: Intensity computation
parameters.description: None | Compute intensity | Compute intensity and power | Compute power (with wavefront curvature).

parameters.name: Material Discontinuity
parameters.description: Default boundary node (refraction/reflection with Fresnel coefficients, thin dielectric films, ideal AR coatings).

parameters.name: Release features
parameters.description: Release from Grid, Release from Boundary, Illuminated Surface, Solar Radiation, Release from Data File.

parameters.name: Wall / Mirror / Grating / Circular or Linear Polarizer / Linear Wave Retarder
parameters.description: Boundary interactions.

parameters.name: Maximum number of secondary rays
parameters.description: Limits ray splitting at discontinuities.

tools.notes: Requires the Ray Optics Module. Rays propagate in time (or optical path length) so the Ray Tracing study needs a time list; unmeshed domains can be traversed ('Optical dispersion' and 'Compute in unmeshed domains' options). Results: Ray Trajectories plot, Spot Diagram, Optical Aberration, Ray (dataset) and the Ray Bin dataset. Ray Acoustics (rac) is the acoustics equivalent.

tools.name: Release from Grid (rays / particles)
tools.description: Release feature in Geometrical Optics, Ray Acoustics and the Particle Tracing interfaces that launches rays/particles from a grid of initial positions (all combinations of x, y, z lists or a random distribution) with a given initial direction (expression, spherical/hemispherical/conical cone with N rays, or from a reference point) and, for rays, an initial phase, intensity and polarization. It is the most common release when the source is not a physical boundary, e.g. collimated beams, point sources and test bundles.
tools.usage: Physics > Geometrical Optics > Release from Grid (relg1); API: physics("gop").create("relg1", "ReleaseGrid", -1)

parameters.name: qx / qy / qz
parameters.description: Initial coordinate lists, e.g. range(-1,0.1,1)[mm].

parameters.name: Ray direction vector
parameters.description: Expression, conical (cone angle, number of rays), spherical, hemispherical, or from point.

parameters.name: Release times
parameters.description: t = 0 or a list, for time-resolved sources.

parameters.name: Initial intensity / power / polarization
parameters.description: When intensity computation is enabled.

tools.notes: Other releases: Release (from domain selection), Release from Boundary, Release from Point, Release from Data File, Illuminated Surface (rays from a source illuminating a surface), Solar Radiation (position/date based sun direction). The number of rays multiplies with cone counts, so start small.

tools.name: Wall (rays)
tools.description: Boundary condition for rays in Geometrical Optics (and for particles in the particle-tracing interfaces) determining what happens on hitting the boundary: Freeze (stop and keep values, the default for detectors), Disappear, Specular reflection, Diffuse scattering, Mixed diffuse and specular, Pass through, or General reflection with a user expression; optionally with a probability of each outcome and secondary rays. Detector planes, apertures, absorbing housings and mirrors are all Wall nodes with different conditions.
tools.usage: Physics > Geometrical Optics > Wall (wall1); API: physics("gop").create("wall1", "Wall", 2); set("WallCondition", "Freeze"|"Stick"|"Disappear"|"Pass"|"SpecularReflection"|"DiffuseScattering"|"IsotropicScattering"|"MixedDiffuseSpecular"|"GeneralReflection")

parameters.name: WallCondition
parameters.description: Freeze | Stick | Disappear | Pass | SpecularReflection | DiffuseScattering | IsotropicScattering | MixedDiffuseSpecular | GeneralReflection (values as stored by COMSOL 6.4).

parameters.name: Reflection probability / secondary ray
parameters.description: Stochastic mixtures and secondary ray emission.

parameters.name: Absorption / attenuation
parameters.description: Intensity reduction per interaction when intensity is computed.

tools.notes: Material Discontinuity handles refraction between meshed media automatically; Mirror is a convenience Wall with specular reflection and coating options. Rays that leave the geometry without hitting a Wall are lost unless the exterior boundary has a Wall.

tools.name: Ray Heating (multiphysics)
tools.description: Multiphysics interface/coupling that combines Geometrical Optics with Heat Transfer in Solids: the absorbed ray power (from the imaginary part of the refractive index or absorbing boundaries) becomes a heat source, and the temperature feeds back into a temperature-dependent refractive index (thermo-optic effect, thermal lensing). Solved with the Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing study, which alternates ray tracing and stationary heat transfer until the fields converge.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Optics > Ray Optics > Ray Heating; or Multiphysics > Ray Heat Source (rhs1); API: multiphysics().create("rhs1", "RayHeatSource", 3); study: Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: gop and ht.

parameters.name: Heat source computation
parameters.description: From ray attenuation in domains and/or boundary absorption.

parameters.name: Number of iterations
parameters.description: Set in the Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing study step.

tools.notes: Requires the Ray Optics Module and, for the ht side, either the core product or the Heat Transfer Module. Intensity computation must be enabled in gop. Adding Solid Mechanics gives stress-optical effects through the Stress-Optical multiphysics coupling.
